facts: Independent company research estimates Infleqtion generated $31.1M of 2025 revenue, up about 10.7% from 2024, and describes H1 2026 revenue of $23.4M, up 74% year over year.

The independent source attributes H1 2026 growth primarily to increased NASA Quantum Gravity Gradiometer activity and reports government customers at approximately 83% of H1 revenue, including 74% from the U.S. government.

The source notes the August 2026 revenue-recognition revision and states that reaching the raised 2026 outlook requires continued contract execution and incremental bookings beyond disclosed remaining performance obligations.
risks: Revenue concentration in government programs creates renewal, appropriations and execution sensitivity.
Raised full-year guidance is not fully covered by disclosed remaining performance obligations and therefore depends on continued execution and additional bookings.
contradictions: Strong reported H1 growth coexists with high government concentration and dependence on future contract execution, so growth should not be treated as diversified commercial validation.
unknowns: This independent source is a research synthesis rather than an audited filing; Alpha should retain issuer/SEC documents as numeric authority and use this artifact as independent corroboration/context.
